title: Why 90% of Canada is Completely Empty

scenes.text: Canada is the second largest country on Earth. Yet almost nobody actually lives there.

lines.en: Canada is the second largest country on Earth.
lines.ko: 캐나다는 지구상에서 두 번째로 큰 나라입니다.

lines.en: Yet almost nobody actually lives there.
lines.ko: 하지만 실제로는 거의 아무도 살지 않습니다.

scenes.text: Draw a line just 100 miles north of the US border. Over 70 percent of all Canadians are squeezed into this tiny strip.

lines.en: Draw a line just 100 miles north of the US border.
lines.ko: 미국 국경에서 북쪽으로 딱 100마일만 선을 그어보세요.

lines.en: Over 70 percent of all Canadians are squeezed into this tiny strip.
lines.ko: 전체 캐나다인의 70% 이상이 이 좁은 띠 안에 몰려 있습니다.

scenes.text: Everything above it? Millions of square miles of empty rock and freezing forest. And the reason isn't just the cold.

lines.en: Everything above it? Millions of square miles of empty rock and freezing forest.
lines.ko: 그 위쪽 전부요? 수백만 제곱마일의 빈 바위와 얼어붙은 숲뿐입니다.

lines.en: And the reason isn't just the cold.
lines.ko: 그리고 그 이유는 단순히 추위 때문만은 아닙니다.

scenes.text: Start with the three northern territories: Yukon, the Northwest Territories, and Nunavut. Together, they cover almost 40 percent of Canada. Yet only about 130,000 people live there. That's less than one percent of the country.

lines.en: Start with the three northern territories: Yukon, the Northwest Territories, and Nunavut.
lines.ko: 북쪽의 세 준주부터 보죠. 유콘, 노스웨스트 준주, 그리고 누나부트입니다.

lines.en: Together, they cover almost 40 percent of Canada.
lines.ko: 이 세 곳을 합치면 캐나다 면적의 거의 40%입니다.

lines.en: Yet only about 130,000 people live there. That's less than one percent of the country.
lines.ko: 그런데 사는 사람은 약 13만 명. 전체 인구의 1%도 안 됩니다.

scenes.text: Nunavut alone is bigger than Mexico. But Mexico has around 130 million people. Nunavut has about 40,000. You could fit everyone into two hockey arenas.

lines.en: Nunavut alone is bigger than Mexico.
lines.ko: 누나부트 하나만 해도 멕시코보다 큽니다.

lines.en: But Mexico has around 130 million people. Nunavut has about 40,000.
lines.ko: 그런데 멕시코 인구는 약 1억 3천만 명, 누나부트는 약 4만 명입니다.

lines.en: You could fit everyone into two hockey arenas.
lines.ko: 하키 경기장 두 곳이면 주민 전부가 들어갑니다.

scenes.text: So where do Canadians actually live? Ontario and Quebec alone hold about 60 percent of the population. All three territories together? Barely a rounding error.

lines.en: So where do Canadians actually live?
lines.ko: 그럼 캐나다 사람들은 실제로 어디에 살까요?

lines.en: Ontario and Quebec alone hold about 60 percent of the population.
lines.ko: 온타리오와 퀘벡 두 주에만 인구의 약 60%가 삽니다.

lines.en: All three territories together? Barely a rounding error.
lines.ko: 세 준주를 다 합쳐도? 반올림 오차 수준입니다.

scenes.text: The first culprit is the Canadian Shield. It's a huge slab of ancient rock that wraps around Hudson Bay. It covers roughly half of the country, and some of its rocks are among the oldest on Earth.

lines.en: The first culprit is the Canadian Shield.
lines.ko: 첫 번째 범인은 캐나다 순상지입니다.

lines.en: It's a huge slab of ancient rock that wraps around Hudson Bay.
lines.ko: 허드슨만을 감싸고 있는 거대한 고대 암반이죠.

lines.en: It covers roughly half of the country, and some of its rocks are among the oldest on Earth.
lines.ko: 국토의 약 절반을 덮고 있고, 그 일부는 지구에서 가장 오래된 암석에 속합니다.

scenes.text: During the last Ice Age, glaciers bulldozed this land and scraped away the soil. What's left is bare rock, thin soil, and countless lakes. Canada has more lakes than any other country on Earth.

lines.en: During the last Ice Age, glaciers bulldozed this land and scraped away the soil.
lines.ko: 마지막 빙하기 동안 빙하가 이 땅을 밀어붙이며 흙을 긁어냈습니다.

lines.en: What's left is bare rock, thin soil, and countless lakes.
lines.ko: 남은 건 맨 바위, 얇은 흙, 그리고 셀 수 없이 많은 호수입니다.

lines.en: Canada has more lakes than any other country on Earth.
lines.ko: 캐나다는 지구상 어느 나라보다 호수가 많습니다.

scenes.text: That makes farming incredibly hard. Only about 7 percent of Canada's land is used as farmland. And without farms, big towns never had a reason to grow.

lines.en: That makes farming incredibly hard.
lines.ko: 그래서 농사가 무척 어렵습니다.

lines.en: Only about 7 percent of Canada's land is used as farmland.
lines.ko: 캐나다 땅 중 농지로 쓰이는 건 약 7%뿐입니다.

lines.en: And without farms, big towns never had a reason to grow.
lines.ko: 농장이 없으니 큰 도시가 생길 이유도 없었죠.

scenes.text: Then there's the cold. Across much of the north, the ground stays frozen all year round. This is permafrost, and it lies beneath roughly half of Canada.

lines.en: Then there's the cold.
lines.ko: 그리고 추위가 있습니다.

lines.en: Across much of the north, the ground stays frozen all year round.
lines.ko: 북쪽 대부분 지역은 땅이 1년 내내 얼어 있습니다.

lines.en: This is permafrost, and it lies beneath roughly half of Canada.
lines.ko: 이것이 영구동토층이고, 캐나다 땅의 약 절반 아래에 깔려 있습니다.

scenes.text: Building anything up there is a nightmare. Roads crack and buckle, pipes freeze, and most supplies have to be flown or shipped in. So in remote northern towns, groceries can cost two or three times more than in the south.

lines.en: Building anything up there is a nightmare.
lines.ko: 그곳에 뭔가를 짓는 건 악몽입니다.

lines.en: Roads crack and buckle, pipes freeze, and most supplies have to be flown or shipped in.
lines.ko: 도로는 갈라지고 휘고, 수도관은 얼고, 물자 대부분은 비행기나 배로 들여와야 합니다.

lines.en: So in remote northern towns, groceries can cost two or three times more than in the south.
lines.ko: 그래서 외딴 북부 마을에선 식료품 값이 남쪽의 두세 배가 되기도 합니다.

scenes.text: History pulled people south as well. In the 1880s, the Canadian Pacific Railway was built close to the border, linking the east to the Pacific. Towns and cities grew up along the tracks.

lines.en: History pulled people south as well.
lines.ko: 역사도 사람들을 남쪽으로 끌어당겼습니다.

lines.en: In the 1880s, the Canadian Pacific Railway was built close to the border, linking the east to the Pacific.
lines.ko: 1880년대, 캐나다 태평양 철도가 국경 가까이에 놓여 동부와 태평양을 이었습니다.

lines.en: Towns and cities grew up along the tracks.
lines.ko: 마을과 도시는 이 철길을 따라 자라났습니다.

scenes.text: The warmest and most fertile land is in the far south, around the Great Lakes and the St. Lawrence River. The corridor from Windsor to Quebec City is home to about half of all Canadians.

lines.en: The warmest and most fertile land is in the far south, around the Great Lakes and the St. Lawrence River.
lines.ko: 가장 따뜻하고 비옥한 땅은 최남단, 오대호와 세인트로렌스강 주변에 있습니다.

lines.en: The corridor from Windsor to Quebec City is home to about half of all Canadians.
lines.ko: 윈저에서 퀘벡시티까지 이어지는 회랑에 캐나다인의 약 절반이 삽니다.

scenes.text: And then there's the United States. Roughly three quarters of Canada's exports go south of the border. Living close to your biggest customer simply makes sense.

lines.en: And then there's the United States.
lines.ko: 그리고 미국이 있습니다.

lines.en: Roughly three quarters of Canada's exports go south of the border.
lines.ko: 캐나다 수출의 약 4분의 3이 국경 너머 남쪽으로 갑니다.

lines.en: Living close to your biggest customer simply makes sense.
lines.ko: 가장 큰 고객 가까이에 사는 건 당연한 선택이죠.

params.heading: THE BIGGEST CUSTOMER
params.label: OF CANADA'S EXPORTS GO TO THE U.S.

scenes.text: So why is 90 percent of Canada so empty? Ancient rock with almost no soil. Ground that never thaws. And a history and economy that pull everyone south.

lines.en: So why is 90 percent of Canada so empty?
lines.ko: 그래서 캐나다의 90%는 왜 이렇게 비어 있을까요?

lines.en: Ancient rock with almost no soil.
lines.ko: 흙이 거의 없는 고대 암반.

lines.en: Ground that never thaws.
lines.ko: 녹지 않는 땅.

lines.en: And a history and economy that pull everyone south.
lines.ko: 그리고 모두를 남쪽으로 끌어당기는 역사와 경제입니다.

scenes.text: The empty north isn't a failure. It's what happens when a country is built on some of the oldest rock on Earth, right next door to the world's biggest economy.

lines.en: The empty north isn't a failure.
lines.ko: 텅 빈 북쪽은 실패가 아닙니다.

lines.en: It's what happens when a country is built on some of the oldest rock on Earth, right next door to the world's biggest economy.
lines.ko: 지구에서 가장 오래된 암반 위에, 세계 최대 경제 대국 바로 옆에 세워진 나라라면 자연스러운 모습이죠.
